hook_text: Four holes in a bottle. Squeeze anywhere and four equal jets fire. That is the law behind every hydraulic machine.
clip_script: Pressure is push spread over area. A pin pierces, a thumb does not, same push, different area. Pascal's principle: squeeze a sealed liquid anywhere and the pressure rises everywhere by the same amount, in every direction, undiminished down any length of pipe. So the bottle with four holes fires four equal jets. The water balloon bulges all over. One master syringe moves four slaves together. Force is pressure times area, so a small master makes a pressure that a big slave turns into a big force. And one brake pedal reaches four wheels at the same instant with the same pressure, so the car stops straight. Pressure is what travels; force is what you get at each end. That is why cars carry two circuits: one leak would empty the lot.
visual_style: Whiteboard bottle with four jets; pressure arrows pointing every way inside a liquid; a pedal, a master cylinder and four wheel cylinders joined by lines; a split pipe and a second circuit.
pacing: Pressure defined, the principle, three demos, the brakes, the two circuits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make the four-hole bottle at home over a sink.
